absent: Numeric encodings of status, syndrome, control, identifier and fault bitfields and masks.
Full layouts of vCPU, arch context, fault record, general registers and reset state.
Locking and concurrency rules except the split-cache slots-lock note.
Callers and sequencing of trap decoders, endianness helpers, reset and control setup.
Semantics of referenced system registers, capabilities, feature predicates and flag operations beyond names.
Error handling beyond top-up allocation failure, empty-cache null and invalid sentinel.

findings.text: Provides conversion from host saved status to 32-bit form that clears two overlapping control positions and reinserts the data-independent-timing indication at its 32-bit location.
Reports whether current guest mode is privileged by interpreting status as 32-bit value compared against user threshold or as 64-bit value compared against EL0.
Centralizes trap-state reads for syndrome, abort address, deferred interrupt status and hypercall immediate from cached per-vCPU fault record.
Fault intermediate address is valid only when non-secure marker present; otherwise an invalid sentinel is returned, else the address field is extracted and page aligned.

Exposes data-abort syndrome interpretations for validity, sanitized non-valid view, extension, width, destination, table-walk indication, write direction, cache maintenance and access size as a power of two.

Classifies traps by instruction length, exception class, instruction-abort identity, execution fault excluding table walks, fault status, conditional value with absent marker, and guest-hypervisor wait traps gated by nesting and EL2 state plus control bits.
Permission versus translation nature follows fault-status predicates; permission granule size is a single bit shifted by a level-derived page-table shift.
Level shift is a fact combining table granularity scaled by distance from level four plus an ordering term.
Flags synchronous and asynchronous external aborts including table-walk and secure variants, and extracts the system-instruction destination register from the syndrome.

Write-fault decision first treats table-walk faults as writes only on permission faults, then excludes instruction aborts, otherwise follows the data write indication, avoiding misclassification of read-only table pages while accepting a double fault with hardware dirty tracking.
Offers short aliases for system-register read and assignment and returns the masked affinity portion of the multiprocessor identifier.
Manages guest endianness by setting a 32-bit status bit or a selected system-control enable, and queries it using hypervisor context and privilege to choose between global and EL0 controls.
Converts a datum between guest and host byte order according to current endianness and length, handling single byte transparently and wider sizes with matching endian helpers.

Counter advance via INCREMENT_PC is forbidden when PENDING_EXCEPTION is set and pend via PENDING_EXCEPTION is forbidden when INCREMENT_PC is set; reset clears pending, mask and advance flags together.

Sanitizes hypervisor trap control by passing through when extended controls are present, else translating trap-all, floating-point, vector and access-related fields into the EL1 view with reserved bits set.

Floating-point and vector trap enable for a guest hypervisor derives from the sanitized enable field where two encodings always trap, one never traps, and one traps only with total-guest-controls set outside EL2, disabled entirely without nesting.

Composes extended hypervisor control from an always-on streaming-vector enable when capable plus feature-gated enables for memory operations, table controls, floating-point, system controls, large-system operations, and nested TLBI relaxation by version and address-support.
Resets a virtual CPU core by zeroing general and floating-point banks plus banked status words and installing supervisor, EL1 or EL2 start status selected by 32-bit state and nesting.

Applies power-state reset by normalizing Thumb entry alignment and mode, propagating caller endianness, installing target address and first argument, and discarding pending exception and counter updates.
Hypervisor memory cache is a singly linked physical head with page count, host-only mapping pointer, and flags word carrying a stage-two accounting option.

Cache behaves as a last-in-first-out stack where push links the supplied page and increments the count, pop on empty returns null else unlinks and decrements, top-up loops until a minimum or allocation failure, and free drains via callback with address translators.

Second-stage context holds a VM identifier, physical table root and table object, host control value, per-CPU last-run marker, eager-split cache and chunk size, owning arch pointer, shadow address and control for invalidation, nested-enable and pending-unmap booleans, and an active-use reference count.
Eager-split page cache and its chunk-size control are guarded by the slots lock of the owning virtual machine.

Two second-stage contexts may share canonical tables when the guest regime is unaffected by its own translation; width reflects guest address size normally and exposed range for shadow; shadow address holds either guest value with shareability cleared or an invalid sentinel; zero reference count means idle with validity carried in the address.

Protected virtual-machine record holds a small handle, two teardown caches for general and stage-two reclaim, and three lifecycle booleans for protected, created and dying where dying bars vCPU loading while allowing page reclaim.

Firmware-call feature state is four bitmap words for standard, hypervisor standard and two vendor ranges; arch memory-slot extension is empty; multiprocessor-index state is a mask plus a flexible compressed-index array.
Compressed index gathers masked affinity bits according to mask width to locate a position in the compressed table.

Facts: halt-poll delay is 500000; maximum vCPUs follows the interrupt-controller limit; feature count is ten with a valid mask covering the low ten positions; manual dirty-log capability combines protect-enable with initially-set; eager-split default is zero; plus stage-two accounting bit, interrupt-controller marker, read-write-lock marker and include guard.

Facts: twelve arch request numbers exist with sleep using wait-without-wakeup semantics and the rest covering interrupts, reset, steal time, redistributor and performance reloads, suspend, counter resync, nested unmap, guest-hypervisor interrupt, virtual control mapping and interrupt-controller update.
Enumerates hypervisor modes default, protected, nested-virtualization and none, with the current-mode query returning none in this build.

Callers must not query permission granule for non-permission faults, must not combine counter advance with pending exception in either direction, must handle the invalid-address sentinel when secure, must handle empty-cache null, and must account for shared tables and cacheable control bits during invalidation.
